D015-D007_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling completely empty for over a year now—like I’m moving through fog. I can’t even pick up a paintbrush anymore, which kills me because art was everything. My thoughts feel slow and cloudy, like I’m always dazed, and I can’t concentrate long enough to sketch, let alone finish a piece. I’ve stopped going to class, stopped seeing friends. I just stay in bed. 

Lately, I’ve been hearing voices—usually a man’s voice telling me I’m a failed artist, that I’ll never matter. Sometimes it says the opposite—that I’m actually a chosen visionary, destined to reveal profound truths through paintings no one’s seen yet. I know it doesn’t make sense, but in the moment, it feels real. These voices only come when I’m deep in this depressive spiral. When I’m not feeling this low, they disappear. 

I’ve thought about ending it—planned it out, actually. There’s a bridge near campus I pass every day. I keep imagining jumping at night when no one’s around. I’ve even timed when the streetlights flicker so I wouldn’t be seen. I don’t want to die, but I don’t know how to keep living like this.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D015-D007_h001.answer: D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h002.question:

Sometimes I get this sudden urge to jump off my balcony, not because I’ve planned it, but like a jolt that pulls me toward the edge. I scare myself.  

It’s important to mention—none of these psychotic-like thoughts or sensations ever happened before this depression hit. When I’m not in this numb, foggy state, I don’t hear voices or believe my body is decaying. They only come with the darkness.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
